newsitem.title: UK: LASMO reports drilling success in Algeria.
newsitem.headline: LASMO reports drilling success in Algeria.

text.p: Oil exploration and production company LASMO Plc on Monday reported success in its drilling operations in Algeria.
LASMO said succesful exploration at the EKT-1 well marks the discovery of a new oil field, while the EME-2 well proved a sucessful appraisal of a previous discovery.

LASMO operates in Algeria through a venture in which it holds a 25 percent stake. Its partners are Anadarko Algeria Corp, which is the operator, and Maersk Olie Algeriet A/S, who both have stakes of respectively 50 and 25 percent.

"EKT-1 is the seventh discovery the partnership has drilled in 10 wildcat wells to date...while the EME-2 appraisal well has provided valuable information that will help us evaluate the size and potential of an existing discovery," said John Hogan, chief operating officer.
The Algerian operations are seen as an area with major potential for LASMO.
Lasmo shares firmed three pence to 219 pence follwing the news. They had already gained sharply last week following speculation of drilling successes.
The EKT-1 well was drilled to a total depth of 3,895 metres.
It flowed at sustained rates of 13,568 barrels of 48.8 degree API oil per day and 8.8 million cubic feet of gas per day. Flowing tubing pressure was 1,067 psi.
The EME-2 well, located about 1.5 km from the EME-1 discovery well, was drilled to a depth of 4,209 metres.
The oil bearing Triassic zone tested at 11,176 barrels of oil per day and 13.9 million cubic feet of gas per day through an equivalent 79/64 inch choke with a flowing tubing pressure of 1,163 psi.
The Devonian zones flowed at a combined rate of 7,351 barrels of condensate per day and 52 million cubic feet of gas per day, LASMO said.
